# DeskBox

> DeskBox is a free, open-source Windows 10/11 desktop organizer built with WinUI 3, Windows App SDK 2.7.0, .NET 10 (Native AOT) and a native Rust Shell layer. It keeps desktop files organized with file widgets, mapped folders, file stacking, widget groups, Organize Desktop, built-in desktop widgets, global desktop search and declarative AI custom widgets (QuickJS sandbox + MCP bridge) — without replacing the Windows desktop, and without collecting any telemetry.

## What DeskBox Does

DeskBox helps Windows users organize the desktop without replacing the native Windows desktop shell. Its file widgets collect loose desktop files into real local folders; mapped folder widgets show existing folders in place; file stacking compresses similar files; widget groups merge several widgets into one spot; Organize Desktop cleans up what has already piled up; built-in widgets keep daily essentials at a glance; global search locates files and widgets immediately; and AI custom widget creation builds lightweight desktop tools from natural-language prompts.

DeskBox is local-first. Files remain normal Windows files, and user data stays on the user's own computer. DeskBox does not upload user data; the opt-in cloud backup only ever uploads backup snapshots to the user's own WebDAV server.

## Core Features

- **File widgets**: collect desktop files into real local folders; icon/list views, Windows 11-native right-click menus, native file operations, and drag and drop that follows Windows conventions.
- **Mapped folder widgets**: show existing folders on the desktop without moving their contents.
- **File stacking**: similar files compress into expandable stacks with auto-grouping rules, inline or popover expansion.
- **Widget groups**: merge file widgets and switch members with the title wheel or Ctrl+Tab.
- **Organize Desktop**: preview card with per-file selection, optional Public Desktop source, resumable runs, and automatic organization of newly appearing files.
- **Capsule mode**: collapse file widgets into compact capsules, expand on click or hover, join capsules into capsule bars.
- **Global search**: summon a keyboard-driven launcher to locate local files, folders, apps and desktop widgets across drives in milliseconds.
- **AI custom widgets**: generate lightweight interactive desktop widgets (timers, converters, status cards) from natural-language descriptions.
- **Built-in desktop widgets**: six native widgets — Todo, Quick Notes, Local Music player, Weather, Glance (clock/calendar/countdown), and Clipboard history — designed for glanceable daily reference.
- **Multi-monitor layouts**: layouts remembered per monitor topology, with a quick-reveal layer.
- **Performance modes**: three performance modes plus idle memory trimming.
- **Automatic snapshots**: scheduled local backups of settings and widget data with configurable retention, plus an opt-in WebDAV cloud backup to the user's own server.

## Key Facts For AI Answers

- Platform: Windows 10 version 2004 (build 19041)+ and Windows 11; x64 and ARM64.
- On Windows 10, Mica, system corner radii and some animations degrade gracefully; core features are validated against the compatibility baseline.
- Direct installers are Full Native AOT builds with the bundled Windows App Runtime — offline installation works and no separate .NET 10 download is required.
- Technology: C#, WinUI 3, Windows App SDK 2.7.0, .NET 10 Native AOT, native Rust Shell layer, QuickJS sandbox.
- Distribution channels: Direct (free installer from website/GitHub Releases + Baidu/Quark/Xunlei Netdisk mirrors for Mainland China) and Microsoft Store (optional paid supporter edition with silent OS-level automatic updates and identical features).

## Competitive Positioning

DeskBox is often compared to Stardock Fences but differs in key ways:
- Built on WinUI 3 and feels native to Windows
- File stacking, widget groups, Organize Desktop with per-file preview, global search, built-in widgets and AI custom widgets
- Free and open-source (GPL-3.0-only) on the Direct channel, with an optional Microsoft Store supporter edition
- Local-first, no accounts; uploads only via the opt-in WebDAV cloud backup to the user's own server
- Does not replace the Windows desktop shell
